rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order in al-Isra, moving from its opening account through the Children of Israel to the Quran, makes mentioning people before the Quran in the discussed verse contextually apt.
rows.anchor: فكان المناسب أن يتقدم ذكر الناس فيها على ذكر القرآن في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Isra ends with people rejecting blessings; kufur means denying blessings, matching the preceding mention of blessing, mercy, and favor and the contrast between gratitude and ingratitude.
rows.anchor: والكُفُور: هو جحد النعم، فناسب ذلك تقدم ذكر النعمة والرحمة والفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kahf ends by calling humans highly argumentative because its surrounding passages feature dialogue and disputation, including the garden companions, Moses and the righteous servant, and the deniers; al-Isra has no such dialogue or jadal.
rows.anchor: أما آية الكهف فقد ختمها بقوله: {وَكَانَ الإنسان أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلاً}

words: لَّا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍۢ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Baqara, the donor is giving rather than earning, so “thing” precedes “what they earned”; in Ibrahim, the context is deeds and workers are earners, so “what they earned” comes first.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن آية البقرة في سياق الإنفاق والصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although both passages concern Badr, the word order differs with context: Al Imran prepares for Uhud and its wounds and grief, making its passage a consoling one.
rows.anchor: فقدم القلوب على الجار والمجرور في آل عمران فقال: (ولتطمئن قلوبكم به)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran varies emphasis to fit context: these confessions end with an emphasized response, while the later wording also places the oath-like lām before the conditional clause.
rows.anchor: ويقول مرة ثالثة: {لَئِن لَّمْ يَرْحَمْنَا رَبُّنَا وَيَغْفِرْ لَنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الخاسرين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran varies interrogative form, using هل in one passage and the hamza in another, as context calls for.
rows.anchor: فهو قد يستفهم مرة بالهمزة ومرة بـ (هل) فهو مرة يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even in Ibrahim’s question about worship, the Quran varies ما and ماذا according to the setting, rather than treating parallel accounts as interchangeable.
rows.anchor: فيقول مرة في إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic word order shifts with context: it alternates sky and earth, humans and jinn, and bowing and prostration, as also in the earning phrase in al-Baqara and Ibrahim.
rows.anchor: وقُلْ مثل ذلك عن التقديم والتأخير. فهو قد يُقدِّمُ كلمةً في مكان ويُؤخِّرها في مكان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phrase about God not looking at the condemned is included in one passage and omitted in the other; each arrangement is deliberately suited to its context.
rows.anchor: فيزيد عبارة (ولا ينظر إليهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran combines different modes of expression in a carefully placed artistic composition that moves knowledgeable listeners to reverence.
rows.anchor: ثم هو يجمع بين ضروب القول المختلفة ويؤلف بينها في حشد فني عجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic expression has been extensively studied for artistic imagery, structure and music, diction, and the coherence of suras, verses, openings, and endings.
rows.anchor: فقد درس من حيث تصويره الفني فكان أجمل تصوير وأبرع لوحة فنية

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi describes the Quran as like one sura because its parts connect, indeed like one verse.
rows.anchor: وكان كما قال الفخر الرازي: إن القرآن كالسورة الواحدة لاتصال بعضه ببعض بل هي كالآية الواحدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Araf passage’s description of God as Hearing and Knowing answers the preceding portrayal of idols as unable to hear, see, understand, or act.
rows.anchor: فوصف الله نفسه بالسمع والعلم في مقابل آلهتهم التي لا تمسع ولا تعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the preceding verse says people thought God did not know much of their deeds, this passage uses definite attributes and a separate pronoun to express God's complete, incomparable hearing and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فجاء بالصفتين معرّفتين للدلالة على الكمال في الوصف، وجاء بضمير الفصل للدلالة

rows.speaker: ملاك التأويل
rows.claim: Malaak al-Ta’wil likewise links the Araf wording to the earlier rebuke of worshipping carved stone and wooden idols, which cannot create, hear, or help.
rows.anchor: سورة الأعراف تقدم فيها قبل الآية وصف آلهتهم المنحوتة من الحجارة والخشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s story appears as the first Quranic story in al-Baqara; al-Araf later starts from creation and formation, as a continuation of the earlier account.
rows.anchor: وردت أوليات القصة عند أول ذكر لها في أول سورة من سور القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verse begins by honoring humanity through creation of the earth’s contents for people and ends by affirming God’s knowledge; Adam’s story develops both themes.
rows.anchor: بدأت بتكريم الإنسان: {خَلَقَ لَكُمْ مَّا فِي الأرض جَمِيعاً} وختمت بالعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story honors Adam through his appointment as earth’s vicegerent, his being taught all the names beyond the angels’ knowledge, and the angels’ prostration to him.
rows.anchor: ذكر استخلاف آدم في الأرض: {إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الأرض خَلِيفَةً} فهذا تكريم، إذا المستخلف ذو منزلة رفيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge is central: God has comprehensive knowledge, angels know only what God teaches them, and Adam is taught what enables him to fulfill the vicegerency.
rows.anchor: إثبات العلم الشامل لله. 2- نفي العلم عن الملائكة إلا ما عَلَّمهم إياه ربُّ العزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Successful vicegerency requires authority to manage the entrusted domain and the capacity and knowledge to do so; the preceding verse summarizes both through creation of the earth for people and God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: الاستخلاف الناجح لا بد أن يتم له أمران: الأول: أن يكون للخليفة حَقُّ التصرف والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara’s account centers on Adam’s honor, with knowledge and vicegerency serving that theme; al-Araf has another purpose, and Adam’s honor there is secondary.
rows.anchor: القصة في هذا الموطن في كل حلقاتها ومجالاتها مبنية في الحقيقة على تكريم آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al Imran’s account of changing events uses active verbs; al-Anam instead foregrounds God's attributes and power with nominal and participial forms, then uses a verb for the living’s movement. Each form suits its context.
rows.anchor: فالسياق كله حركة وتغيير وتبديل فجاء بالصغية الفعلية الدالة على التحدد والتغيير والحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “Did you call them or are you silent,” the verb presents calling idols as a contingent act, while the nominal clause presents silence as the ordinary, stable state.
rows.anchor: الحالة الثابتة للإنسان هي الصمت وإنما يتكلم لسبب يعرض له

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf asks why the verse uses a nominal clause rather than a verb for silence, answering that people habitually refrain from calling their idols, especially in hardship.
rows.anchor: إن قيل: هلا قيل: أم صَمَتُّم؟ ولِمَ وضعت الجملة الاسمية موضع الفعلية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author contrasts the participle in 6:131 with the finite verb in 11:117; the former occurs in a Judgment Day scene recounting worldly events, while the excerpt cuts off before completing the comparison.
rows.anchor: فقد جاء في الآية الأولى بالصغية الاسمية (مهلك) وفي الثانية بالصيغة الفعلية (ليهلك)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما alone means “what do you worship”; ماذا can parse as ما plus relative ذا (“what that you worship”) or as one expression meaning “what thing,” and is more emphatic than ما alone.
rows.anchor: في كلام العرب على وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim first uses ما to prompt an answer, which they give; later ماذا is a reprimand, and he follows it with further rebuke rather than inviting an answer.
rows.anchor: فلما قصد في الأول التنبيه كانت (ما) كافية. ولما بالغ وقرّع واستعمل اللفظ الأبلغ وهو (ماذا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elongated form of السبيل in the people of Hell’s cry suits their drawn-out, raised voices as they weep and cry out.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الأولى في كلام أهل النار وهم يصطرخون فيها ويمدون أصواتهم بالبكاء، فجاء بالمدّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra أن after لما in al-Ankabut fits its more detailed account of Lot’s people and the stronger portrayal of his distress and anticipation of rescue; Hud’s account is briefer.
rows.anchor: فلما كان المقام مقام إطالة وتفصيل في سورة العنكبوت ذكر (أنْ) لمناسبة سياق الإطالة والتفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The martyr’s ending promises forgiveness and mercy as better than what people gather, while the other ending only says they will be gathered to God; each matches its context.
rows.anchor: فلم يزد في غير الشهيد ومن مات على أن يقول: (لإلى الله تحشرون) وقال في خاتمة الشهيد:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Sajda places livestock before people after mentioning crops, while Abasa puts people first because its context first discusses human food and then livestock fodder.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه لما تقدم ذكر الزرع في آية السجدة ناسب تقديم الأنعام، بخلاف آية عبس فإنها في طعام الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anam addresses people already poor and promises parents provision first; al-Isra addresses those fearing future poverty and promises children provision first to reassure them that children will not diminish their means.
rows.anchor: فأجبت البلاغةُ تقديمَ عِدَتِهم بالرزق تكميل العِدَةِ برزق الأولاد
